title: A Revolution of R.P.G Maker MZ and also maby older versions.

posts.author: oliveric
posts.body:
I don't know if I'm posting this in the right thread, so sorry if I got it wrong the first time here.
Here's what I think would take the whole engine and also community by storm.
If you simply had an official (or indie-developer-made) plugin set that allowed you to fully build sprites yourself, within the engine.
And I don't mean just the simple things we have right now as it relates to window makers and cut-scene helpers and such as add-on options.
What I mean is that what every single person who makes a game will want is custom characters and items and so on.
So if we simply had a plugin that was wildly "broad" with hundreds of templates and so on to colour yourself - you could have for example a sprite making engine that would easily enable you to export and create custom sprites for Sword animations for example. Instead of having to do it yourself in ms paint or the alike, photoshop maby, you could have an engine that simply allowed you to create your sword, and then automatically pump out all the sprite sheets for the sword attack animation, using that particular sword, and for all of your chosen characters. Same with helmets, armour, items, animations maby - and all of that and all of it.
The funny thing here is that I know that the technical know how to create such a plugin would be within the scope of hundreds if not thousands of developers already. A customizeable sprite sheet program must fall way below most other new game projects in difficulty. I'm talking about proffestionals and hardcore indie devs.
And why is it funny? Because everybody would love this. I think every single customer for R.P.G maker would buy this instantly, if it was all-encompassing.
A sprite sheet generator in-game. For all the objects and so on.
And so the economic potential here would probably basically sky-rocket in comparison to any other idea here.
Am I wrong?
Does anybody here agree? If you would make such a thing to completion - know that at least I would buy it instantly.
All the love.
And one more thing:
Maby this one is actually targeted at the official dev's at R.P.G Maker itself:
If you made a new version of R.P.G Maker that allowed us to create combat on-screen that simply makes you start attacking continously what you are clicking on once, (If it is an enemy assigned as a possible target) - then the same engine would be able to reach so many more people who are not looking into creating R.P.G's with turn-based combat.
You could make your engine capable of supplying what in my mind would sound like twice as many possible games, but with EASE of doing them.
(Like Old-School Runescape, or basically all MMO's - you click a target, and your character starts auto-attacking - also juicy of course if magic and ranged attacks would be as easy to set up in this way with projectiles and so on.)
So to the game dev's at R.P.G Maker MZ & Older versions - I think you could get a huge increase in customers through making the "clicker" - on screen combat availible easily.
And I think that the nieche for R.P.G maker is the FEEL of it. It is just SO incredibly amazingly fluffingly nice to work with for somebody like me who has NO experience in coding and so on.
And to any indie-dev out there - if you would simply create a sprite-sheet creator with huge intrinsic templates with all items needed, like armour weapons, and helmets and even spell projectiles for magic and so on - I think if that product would be made and would be natural enough to use and be able to provide you with then that customized sword of your own, but now with one or two clicks also now that sword exists as the animation sheet for your character sprite-sheet - then you'd get rich. I think. I'll make you as rich anyways as buying your plugin would cost!
Best Wishes and regards - An R.P.G Maker lover but also dreamer of what would "complete" the engine for me.

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body:
There are already 3rd party character generators with weapon animations. I use Time Elements which is official DLC and there are other like LPC which is free.
As for on screen auto-attacking, you can do it with free ABS plugins like Chrono Engine and I've written extensive guides on it. You can check the YouTube link in my sig to see for yourself what it can do. Or QJ Bullet/Map Projectiles, also free.
I will tell you that RPG Maker isn't really great for this type of gameplay, though. It's far easier and smoother to do in another engine like GDevelop which is far more flexible in what kind of games you can make and also an easy, no-code engine.
If you do it in RPG Maker there is just a lot more work and "fighting with the engine" to make it do things it doesnt natively support, and may lead you to buying expensive plugins trying to recreate features that other engines just offer built in for free and are natively supported by their engine devs and community.
Look at sample games made in other engines where that and other types of games are common and nothing special, and the users churn them out with ease.
The RPG Maker Devs do have "Action Game Maker" coming out next month you can keep an eye on, but know there are already established engines that have offered these features for years. Action Game Maker itself piggybacks on the more-established Godot just like RPG Maker Unite piggybacked on Unity. Tells you all you need to know, really.

posts.author: SGHarlekin
posts.body:
Pretty unrealistic this "generator for everything" if not borderline impossible. These generators exist, but are bound to the artstyle the creator or their collaborative artists are using. To create such a thing is not necessarily a coding problem. Again, third party generators exist.
What you're asking for is almost infinite art to generate all these things, which will just never happen. I don't see how, or why potentially thousands of artists should come together to throw together all this art.
Then you'd have such an overwhelmingly complex generator, with thousands of templates and artstyle, it would likely become cumbersome to use. Great games are great in part due to amazing sprite work. All the great 2d rpgs have very expressive sprites with animations and poses you just won't get in a generator. (Which is why all the default can do is walk)
Sure, it's a nice dream to have "everything" at your fingertips at the push of a button, but it's unrealistic.

My videos show autoattacking. I didn't include touch to select target but it's possible with a short script.
Personally though, if I were to do it again I would use a different engine as I said earlier. The pathfinding, collision and performance are just a lot better in other engines. RPG Maker is not really built for that type of gameplay, you can do it but the performance will be worse and clunkier than if you used an engine built for it.
RPG Maker is not the only no-code engine. Do your homework. I just recommend GDevelop because it's free and you can try it yourself for no risk.
